The following is a list of the 67 [counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)") ([Pennsylvania German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_German_language "Pennsylvania German language"): _Kaundis_, singular _Kaundi_) of the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). The city of [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") is coterminous with [Philadelphia County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_County,_Pennsylvania "Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania"), the municipalities having been consolidated in 1854, and all remaining county government functions having been merged into the city after a [1951 referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1951_Philadelphia_municipal_election#Referendum "1951 Philadelphia municipal election").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Pennsylvania#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Pennsylvania#cite_note-2) Eight of the ten most populous counties are in the [southeastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_metropolitan_area "Philadelphia metropolitan area") portion of the state, including four of the top five, and eight of the top ten most populous counties are in either the [Greater Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_metropolitan_area "Philadelphia metropolitan area") or [Greater Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Pittsburgh "Greater Pittsburgh")[metropolitan statistical areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area").

The [Federal Information Processing Standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Information_Processing_Standards "Federal Information Processing Standards") (FIPS) code, used by the [U.S. government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States") to uniquely identify counties, is provided with each entry. FIPS codes are five-digit numbers; for Pennsylvania the codes start with 42 and are completed with the three-digit county code. The FIPS code for each county in the table links to census data for the specific county.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Pennsylvania#cite_note-epa-3)

The following is a list of the 67 [counties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)") ([Pennsylvania German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_German_language "Pennsylvania German language"): _Kaundis_, singular _Kaundi_) of the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). The city of [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") is coterminous with [Philadelphia County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_County,_Pennsylvania "Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania"), the municipalities having been consolidated in 1854, and all remaining county government functions having been merged into the city after a [1951 referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1951_Philadelphia_municipal_election#Referendum "1951 Philadelphia municipal election").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Pennsylvania#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Pennsylvania#cite_note-2) Eight of the ten most populous counties are in the [southeastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_metropolitan_area "Philadelphia metropolitan area") portion of the state, including four of the top five, and eight of the top ten most populous counties are in either the [Greater Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_metropolitan_area "Philadelphia metropolitan area") or [Greater Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Pittsburgh "Greater Pittsburgh")[metropolitan statistical areas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area").

The [Federal Information Processing Standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Information_Processing_Standards "Federal Information Processing Standards") (FIPS) code, used by the [U.S. government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States") to uniquely identify counties, is provided with each entry. FIPS codes are five-digit numbers; for Pennsylvania the codes start with 42 and are completed with the three-digit county code. The FIPS code for each county in the table links to census data for the specific county.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Pennsylvania#cite_note-epa-3)
